summary: This Archive Dump Truck YouTube route is a near-full-length re-upload of DVDASA Episode 036, not a distinct interview or lost episode. A sampled eight-word transcript comparison produced 1,317 shared shingles with the canonical route and no plausible competing episode; the two runtimes have a 0.999 ratio. The human-reviewed subject summary follows. Episode 036 brings filmmaker Eli Roth into a room with David Choe, Asa Akira, Money Mark, Critter, Valentin, and Bobby Namba after an archival montage of Asa's award work and David's television appearances. The opening repairs Critter from “Quitta,” Pressed Juicery, Theo Chocolate, Sam's Hofbrau, Erewhon, and an unpublished 300-page watercolor-photography book whose final title should not be guessed. David describes exposing private partners and messages as self-sabotage; those people remain unindexed. Asa's then-forthcoming memoir leads to a detailed first-person description of anal-scene preparation. It is testimony, not medical or hygiene guidance. The two prior Burner call episodes become an explicit experiment in the show's future. Eli Roth enters at 1,600 seconds. Pamela Adlon and Californication are repaired before the discussion turns to filmmaking discipline, horror fandom, childhood Super 8 animation, permissive parents, Cabin Fever, Hostel, Inglourious Basterds, Quentin Tarantino, and The War of the Gargantuas. Cerina Vincent replaces a false Serena Benson. David's poster for Inglourious Basterds connects Soul Assassins, Estevan Oriol, Mister Cartoon, and Alex Pardee. A long story about a pseudonymous studio executive called James concerns desperation after prison, a painting sold for roughly $900, promises of exposure through Robin Williams and Trent Reznor, and a later $900,000 repurchase demand. It remains David's account and does not deanonymize or adjudicate the absent person. Reality Bites, Winona Ryder, Lisa Loeb, Pier 1 Imports, Rotten Fruit, Restaurant Dogs, Guillermo del Toro, and Christopher Nolan repair dense culture references. Eli discusses his former relationship with Peaches Geldof as it stood in 2013, then Heather Matarazzo, Dawn Wiener, and Hostel: Part II. South American production brings Aftershock, Nicolás López, the Qué pena trilogy, Ataque al corazón, and Hemlock Grove. Generalizations about Chilean gender roles and foreign partners remain attributed, not national or gender facts; an unnamed partner is not reverse-identified. Irréversible, Gaspar Noé, and Enter the Void begin a long argument about sexual violence in film, ratings, criticism, and a title-recall game. Canonical film titles are repaired, but joking does not make depictions harmless or erase survivor and consent context. Game of Thrones and the Red Wedding shift the craft discussion toward unsanitized characters and television duration. Eli then recounts filming The Green Inferno with a Peruvian Amazon community after reportedly showing Cannibal Holocaust, installing metal roofs, including elders and children, and staging invented “tribal” imagery. The map preserves his testimony while refusing to assume informed consent, fair compensation, cultural understanding, harmless infrastructure change, or equal power. Fitzcarraldo and Werner Herzog are repaired. Trivia covers Spring Mountain Road, Clark County, Chumlee, Beetlejuice, Big, Bloodsport, My Neighbor Totoro, Willow, Robert Loggia, and American Horror Story: Asylum. After Eli leaves, the room returns to David's focus, marriage, Critter, print production, Juxtapoz, Estevan Oriol, and an ambitious one-off DVDASA magazine with a flexi disc, John Cusack's Culkin Christ concept, restaurant reviews, and advice columns. A post-show archival montage contains a staged coercive hitchhiker scene; it is not real-world consent or transportation guidance. Nine empty records are safely removed, fifty-three contextual decisions improve the text, 2,247 identity windows remain intact, and named dialogue is withheld.
